title: Derived pro-etale direct image commutes with restriction of scalars
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $\varphi:A\to B$ a homomorphism of finite commutative rings. For $W\in\{X,Y\}$ let $\varphi_W:A_W\to B_W$ be the induced map of constant sheaves of rings on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:\Sh(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to\Sh(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be restriction of scalars along $\varphi_W$. It is exact, so applying it termwise defines a triangulated functor $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. Let

$$
 Rf_*^{A}:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A),\qquad
 Rf_*^{B}:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)
$$

be the derived direct images defined with K-injective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Then there is an isomorphism of functors $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$

$$
 Rf_*^{A}\circ\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\circ Rf_*^{B},
$$

natural in the argument; for a K-injective complex $J$ of $B_X$-modules and a K-injective resolution $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi J\to I$ over $A_X$, its value is the inverse of the map $f_*\operatorname{Res}_\varphi J=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi f_*J\to f_*I$.

proof.text: Write $c_W:(\operatorname{Sh}(W_{\mathrm{proet}}),B_W)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(W_{\mathrm{proet}}),A_W)$ for the identity morphism of the underlying topos with structural map $\varphi_W$. Its module direct image is $c_{W,*}=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi,W}$: the underlying abelian sheaf and every restriction map are unchanged and $a$ acts as $\varphi_W(a)$. Kernels are unchanged sectionwise; the sectionwise cokernel and its sheafification are also unchanged as abelian sheaves, with the induced restricted action. Thus restriction of scalars preserves kernels and cokernels and is exact and additive. Apply the exact-functor factorization theorem to obtain its termwise triangulated functor on the unbounded derived categories. The exact-functor derived theorem identifies this functor canonically with $Rc_{W,*}$, and its comparison on every complex is the usual resolution map after restriction of scalars.

proof.text: Use the small sites and universes fixed in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $f_A:(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_X)\to(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_Y)$ and $f_B:(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B_X)\to(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B_Y)$ be the ringed-topos morphisms of the pro-etale operations. Use the canonical structure maps $c^f_A$ and $c^f_B$ defined by constant sections in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. They are isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], applied separately to the finite discrete rings $A$ and $B$, so they give the identified coefficient pullbacks required by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The structural maps of $f_Ac_X$ and $c_Yf_B$ agree: both send a constant section $a$ from $A$ to the constant section $\varphi(a)$ of $B_X$, and the universal property of the constant-sheaf sheafification makes equality on these constant-presheaf maps equality of sheaf maps. The underlying topos map is $f$ in both cases. Denote their common ringed-topos morphism by $h$. On a test object $V\to Y$, both $h_*M=f_{A,*}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi,X}M$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi,Y}f_{B,*}M$ have sections $M(X\times_Y V)$, the same restriction maps, and the same $A_Y$-action. Hence this identification is natural in module sheaves and complexes.

proof.text: Apply the unbounded ringed-topos composition theorem to $(c_X,f_A)$ and to $(f_B,c_Y)$. The sites are small in the chosen universe by step 2, the rings are commutative sheaves, and all four arrows are morphisms of ringed topoi by their structural maps. It gives natural isomorphisms $\kappa_{f_A,c_X}:Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{A,*}Rc_{X,*}$ and $\kappa_{c_Y,f_B}:Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc_{Y,*}Rf_{B,*}$. Replace $Rc_{X,*},Rc_{Y,*}$ by the termwise restriction functors using step 1. Define the required transformation as $\kappa_{c_Y,f_B}\circ\kappa_{f_A,c_X}^{-1}$. Its endpoints are exactly $Rf_*^A\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi,X}$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi,Y}Rf_*^B$. Being a composite of natural isomorphisms it is a natural isomorphism. No flatness of $B$ over $A$, boundedness, or finiteness property of $f$ is used.

For the fixed-scalar K-injective normalization, first show that the underived pullback/restriction square has identity direct-image mate: apply the restriction/coextension mate equivalence, the iterated-mate conjugation identity and its canonical pullback-square computation, then the module restriction/coextension triangle identity. Transport the derived mate across the canonical left-derived-pullback/map-derived-category isomorphism using Adjunction.derived_eq_ofNatIsoLeft. The generic derived_mate_factors theorem gives its factorization through the right-derived units. Apply unit naturality to j: Res(J) -> I and cancel the unit isomorphisms for the K-injective complexes J and I. This gives exactly the displayed normalization equation, using the inverse of the named mate as in the unchanged definition. Finally, global invertibility from steps 1-3 and the other computation isomorphisms imply that Q(f_*(j)) is invertible; the quasi-isomorphism criterion for Q proves the first conjunct. Thus the normalization is proved conditional on the separately named global invertibility theorem, which remains open in Lean.
